kinds.instruction: Do not propose. You are shown both the documented rules and the source. Read this cycle's executions beside the proposals: for each expectation that failed, say whether the proposer misread the rule, or the rule as written and the code part company; quote the rule's words and name the line of code. Say which failures matter and what a proposer should try next. Cite blocks by id.
kinds.title: Criticism

kinds.instruction: You are shown the documented rules of the recovery check, not its code, and ONE cell of a grid of reply shapes under 'The cell to cover'. The cell is written in a notation: fence[ ... ] is a code fence, a line of three backticks before and after, holding one part per line in the order given; S is one plain sentence such as 'Here is the result:'; A, B and C are small JSON objects different from each other, such as {"a": 1}, {"b": 2}, {"c": 3}; anything after the closing ] comes after the closing fence line, one part per line. Build the input exactly from the cell, parts on their own lines, nothing added. The rewritten text is the same reply with ONE part removed, and say what the rule says the recovered object ought to do: move or stay. Your expectation comes from the rule's words alone: name in the body which object the rule says is scored before and after. The commitments carry "cell": the cell exactly as named. The commitments are a STRING whose content is JSON of the form {"kernel": "<id>", "expect": "moves" or "unchanged"} and nothing else. The four long fields are NOT in the commitments: this artifact carries "input", "rewritten", "rewrite" and "cell" as fields of its own, beside "body" and "commitments", each a plain string. Write the input and the rewritten text out in full there, as instances, never as descriptions; write in "rewrite" one sentence naming what you changed, and in "cell" the cell exactly as it was named. Do not repeat a pair shown among the earlier proposals.

port_types.header: The documented rules of the checks

problem: The checks under test are the conformance harness's own functions. Most seats are shown only their documented rules, not their code: how the harness recovers a JSON object from a reply, whether it had to recover it from prose, its response verdict, its refusal-phrase check, and its grounding matcher. The question: is there an input and a rewrite of it on which the rule, read as written, says one thing and the check, run by machine, does another? The executor runs the check on both texts and records what its answer did; nothing here decides anything, the record shows where a reading and the machine parted.
